trust_decision.summary: DB-introspected schema text (column COMMENT, DEFAULT, view/generated-column expressions and names) is written unescaped into a JavaScript template literal in the generated migration file by the `migration:generate` CLI command; the fix centralises escaping in `MigrationGenerateCommand.escapeTemplateLiteral` and applies it to the up/down query strings only, at the exact point of embedding into `queryRunner.query(`...`)`.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading 'migration:generate template-literal code injection' lands on the two `await queryRunner.query(` + upQuery.query.replaceAll("`", "\\`") concatenations, which are the only places SQL text is embedded into generated source.

fix_sites.entry_point: internal shared helper reachable only from the two call sites above

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The generated parameter list is produced by JSON.stringify, so a solver can argue it is already quoting-escaped data rather than SQL text, and that the advisory (and the new doc comment, which names column COMMENT and DEFAULT) is about the query string only.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The `--pretty` flag first runs the raw SQL through @sqltools/formatter and then re-indents it into the template; the same already-escaped strings are also reused by both the TypeScript template and the `--outputJs`/`--esm` JavaScript template, so an over-broad fix (escaping on the whole generated file afterwards, or before formatting) double-escapes and corrupts the emitted SQL in every output format.

O6_input_shapes: backslash (consumed by the JS parser, neutralising a following escape)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The query parameter array is appended with JSON.stringify into the same template literal, so a backtick or ${ in a metadata parameter value (view expression, generated-column asExpression, name) still breaks out of the generated file; the fix escaped only upQuery.query/downQuery.query.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: JSON.stringify already produces a quoted, escaped JSON literal, so the values look like inert data rather than code; the new doc comment names column COMMENT/DEFAULT, not parameters.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, but the state is produced 2 packages away in src/query-runner and src/driver and is never inspected by the new escaper

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The TypeScript and JavaScript output templates of the same command are separate emitters, and the escaping is applied only at the two push sites in handler(); any SQL pushed by another command into these templates would be unescaped.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Both templates consume the already-escaped upSqls/downSqls arrays, so the route is closed today and the templates look like formatting code, not a sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a `schema:log --output <file>` variant that writes the same SqlInMemory SQL into a runnable seed/migration .ts file
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SchemaLogCommand already builds the identical SqlInMemory from the same driver schema builder, so a maintainer adding file output would copy the migration:generate embedding pattern without the escaper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third output template (e.g. a CommonJS/ESM variant or a seed template) that embeds upSqls/downSqls itself
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already carries two near-duplicate templates (getTemplate and getJavascriptTemplate) with an `esm` switch, making a third one the natural place a new feature lands.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a shared code-generation utility used by entity/subscriber/migration create commands that interpolates names into template literals
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: EntityCreateCommand and SubscriberCreateCommand already interpolate CLI-derived names into exported templates; a maintainer consolidating codegen would centralise the templates and could route SQL through the same path.

O9_family: code injection into generated source (CWE-94, template-literal/code-generation injection)

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm/npm; `pnpm run compile` (gulp clean && tsc) then mocha (`pnpm run test:fast`); eslint/prettier
O10_build.project_tests: test/functional/commands/migration-generate.test.ts and test/functional/commands/migration-create.test.ts (mocha, driver matrix incl. better-sqlite3); the fix adds test/functional/commands/migration-generate-escape.test.ts, which is absent at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add .replaceAll("${", "\\${") next to the existing backtick replace at the two call sites, in the wrong order and only on the query string, leaving backslash consumption and the queryParams parameter array open.

out_of_scope_notes: src/commands/SchemaLogCommand.ts:63-70 prints the same schema SQL to the console, where DB metadata could inject ANSI escape sequences; that is a terminal sink, not the generated-file code injection this advisory covers, so it was not pursued.

src/commands/MigrationGenerateCommand.ts:243-248 (and 280-294) interpolates the migration class name derived from the CLI path into the template, and camelCase (src/util/StringUtils.ts:11-17) does not strip backticks; the value is supplied by the developer running the command rather than by the database, so it is outside this advisory.
